subject: Dedicated capacity - integration & autoscaling follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@hyperdocs.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com, alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity - integration & autoscaling follow-up

Sam - great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so we can line up a technical deep dive:  

Summary of what we heard (please correct me if I missed anything):
- Primary use: real-time document ingestion + semantic search and a generation service that synthesizes short answers (300-500 tokens).
- Required features: embeddings + reranker for top-N, structured output / tool calling for citations, and routing policies (latency-sensitive for the QA path, cost-optimized for async batch jobs).
- Deployment preference: Dedicated capacity (VPC) with static egress IPs and SAML/OAuth2 integration for your tooling.
- SLA/scale: target steady-state ~70 concurrent requests, peak bursts ~200-250 req/s during ingest spikes; average output ~350 tokens.

Open questions for HyperDocs (if you can confirm before the deep-dive):
1) Peak QPS and burst duration (minutes/hours)?
2) Typical and max tokens in inputs (avg and 95th pct) - affects KV cache sizing.
3) Do you plan to use client-side streaming vs server-side streaming?
4) Any egress/firewall constraints (IP allowlist, NAT/GW)?

What we'll bring to the technical deep-dive (Aditya + Alex will join):
- SDK initialization and recommended auth flows (API keys vs mTLS vs token exchange).
- Routing policy examples: latency-first vs cost-first, and canary rules across model variants.
- Structured output / tool-calling examples and how we surface tool results in the response stream.
- Embeddings + reranker architecture: indexing, batching, and suggestions on recall/latency tradeoffs.
- Autoscaling and queue sizing: recommended starting config, per-node throughput assumptions, concurrency limits, and burst capacity settings.

Attachments: redwood_map_hyperdocs_v1.pdf (draft MAP) and dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (template for your traffic numbers)

Proposed slots for the deep dive (PT): Tue Jul 20 09:00-10:00, Wed Jul 21 11:00-12:00. Let me know what works.

Thanks - looking forward to the next step.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - integration & autoscaling follow-up

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and clarifications from our side:  

Answers to your questions:
1) Peak bursts are usually 10-20 minutes during heavy indexing runs, occasional longer spikes (up to 90 minutes) during major releases. Peak QPS observed: ~220 rps.
2) Input tokens: avg ~120 tokens; output tokens avg ~350; 95th pct output ~650. We also do multi-turn contexts that push history to ~1.5k tokens for some sessions.
3) We prefer server-side streaming for the interactive UI.
4) We will be in an AWS VPC with NAT; we can provide a short list of static egress IPs or work with VPC peering if needed.

Other notes:
- We want embeddings for semantic search (approx 10M docs), initial index build will be batched overnight. Reranker will run top-50 -> top-5 re-rank during query time. Latency SLA for query path: p95 < 250ms end-to-end if possible.
- Security: we need OAuth2 SSO for users and are open to either short-lived tokens from our auth service or long-lived API keys scoped to the dedicated cluster.

Slot: Tue Jul 20 09:00 PT works for our team. Please send the invite.

I'll attach a short CSV with sample payloads in a follow-up - that should help with sizing.

Thanks,
Sam Carter
Head of Platform - HyperDocs
sam.carter@hyperdocs.ai

From: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - integration & autoscaling follow-up (tech notes)

Thanks for the details, Sam - helpful. A few technical notes and initial recommendations ahead of Tue's deep-dive:  

Auth & SDK:
- SDK init (high-level):
  - Python/Node SDKs support either API key, short-lived token exchange (recommended for per-user scoping), or mTLS for higher security.
  - Example (pseudocode):
    client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<REDACTED>")
    client.configure(region="us-west-2", routing_profile="latency-first")

Routing & canarying:
- Routing policies can be per-route or per-customer. You can do latency-first for query endpoints and cost-first for background batch jobs.
- Canarying across model variants is supported (percentage rollout + health checks). We recommend starting with 5% traffic to new model variants for 24-48 hours.

Structured output / tool calling:
- We support structured JSON outputs + tool-calling primitives. For tool calls we stream a tool-invocation object followed by the tool response; SDK exposes hooks to run local tools or remote services and return results into the generation context.

Embeddings & reranker:
- For your ~10M docs index, we suggest a two-stage approach: dense embeddings for candidate retrieval (ann index) + lightweight transformer reranker for top-N precision.
- We recommend batching embedding ingests (200-500 docs/batch) during the overnight index job to keep GPU throughput high.

Autoscaling & sizing (initial guidance):
- Assumptions: model variant X (production-recommended), median response 350 tokens (decode cost), average reqs per second target = 200 peak.
- Throughput per GPU (approx): 50-60 req/s for the requested model at your token sizes (will vary by kernel/quant).
- Concurrency per node: 16 active concurrent requests (you can tune based on latency SLOs).
- Starting deployment: 3 GPU nodes (handles sustained ~150 req/s) + burst pool of 2 nodes for short spikes (burst capacity kicks in automatically).
- Queue sizing: we recommend a request queue with soft concurrency limit and a max queue wait of 2500ms for low-latency paths; longer for batch jobs.
- Autoscale policy: scale on both queued requests and backend GPU utilization; set cooldowns to avoid oscillation during short spikes (30-60s).

Next steps before Tue:
- If you can upload the sample CSV (as mentioned), we'll fill the dedicated-sizing template with estimated node counts and expected monthly token consumption.
- We'll also share a brief load-test plan and a proposed canary rollout schedule. Attached: dedicated-sizing-filled.xlsx (preliminary, will update after your CSV).

If you want, we can also run a short PoC load test against a preview cluster once we have the sample payloads and an allowlist for IPs.
